findings.title: enableSqlExpressions has inverted, dead logic that is a trap for future edits
findings.body: The helper computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (so `enabled` is true precisely when the feature flag is OFF) and then returns `false` from both branches. The function behaves as intended today (always disabled), but the variable name has the opposite meaning of its value, and the `if enabled { return false }` branch is dead code. The obvious future 'fix' of changing the final line to `return enabled` would re-enable SQL expressions exactly when the flag is disabled, i.e. for every default installation. If the intent is a hard kill-switch, make that explicit (e.g. `return false` with a comment referencing the CVE) rather than leaving an inverted, no-op flag check in place.

findings.title: No regression test asserting SQL expressions are rejected even with the feature flag enabled
findings.body: This PR is the in-repo fix for a critical RCE/LFI (CVE-2024-9264), yet it adds no test. There is nothing verifying that `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` returns an error for `QueryTypeSQL` when `FlagSqlExpressions` is enabled, nor that the legacy path (`UnmarshalSQLCommand` -> `NewSQLCommand` -> `sql.TablesList`) fails and never reaches `QueryFramesInto`. The legacy path is only protected implicitly by the stub `DB` returning 'not implemented'; if someone later restores a working `DB` implementation (or swaps in a different engine), the legacy `/api/ds/query` path would silently become live again with no explicit guard and no failing test to catch it. A unit test with the flag forced on, for both entry points, would lock in the fix.

findings.title: Every SQL expression attempt now unconditionally emits an Error-level log with the raw SQL
findings.body: Because the stub `DB.RunCommands` always returns 'not implemented', `TablesList` now hits the `logger.Error("error serializing sql", ...)` branch on every call, logging the full user-supplied SQL and the fabricated `SELECT json_serialize_sql(...)` command at Error level, followed by a second Warn log in `NewSQLCommand`. For a feature that is intentionally disabled, any user selecting the SQL expression type (still visible in the UI when the flag is on) will generate misleading error-level noise that looks like an internal failure rather than an intentional rejection. The disabled path should short-circuit with a single clear message before attempting to 'serialize' anything, or at least log at a lower level.

findings.title: User-facing error text misrepresents a deliberate security disablement as 'not implemented'
findings.body: The new guard returns `sqlExpressions is not implemented`, and the legacy path surfaces `error reading SQL command` (via the stubbed `TablesList`). Both messages suggest a missing or malformed feature rather than an intentional removal. Operators who enabled the still-registered `sqlExpressions` feature toggle (whose docs are untouched by this PR) will get contradictory signals: the flag exists and is documented, the UI offers the expression type, but every query fails with a message implying incomplete code. A message stating that SQL expressions are disabled (ideally with a reference to the security advisory) would avoid confusion and support tickets.
